title: How MarketPulse Reaches Every Verdict
philosophy: Every number shown is computed deterministically from public market data — the AI never invents one.
The AI's only job is to translate these numbers into plain English. The verdict comes from math, not the model.
Nothing here is investment advice, a prediction, or a recommendation. It is a snapshot of the current environment, always shown with its evidence.

regime_model.description: A weighted score blends four price/volume factors plus a capped news modifier into a 0-100 scale, mapped to Bullish / Bearish / Neutral / Uncertain.
regime_model.scale: Raw factor scores live in [-1, +1]; the blend maps to 0-100 via (raw+1)/2*100.
regime_model.why_these_weights: Trend is heaviest because the position of price relative to its moving averages is the most stable beginner-readable signal. Momentum and volatility are equal co-factors: one measures direction strength, the other measures reliability of that direction. Volume confirms whether moves are broadly participated. News is capped at ±10% so headlines can influence — never dominate — the math.

verdict_mapping.uncertain: realized volatility above 28% annualized pushes the read here regardless of direction

regime_model.confidence: Directional confidence is dampened as realized volatility rises above 28%; neutral and uncertain verdicts are additionally capped (60% and 55% respectively) so the UI never overstates them.

indicators.name: Simple Moving Averages (20/50/200)
indicators.origin: Standard practice in technical analysis for over a century
indicators.what: The average close of the last N days, redrawn daily.
indicators.why: Price above its 50-day average is the most beginner-readable trend marker; the 200-day separates long-term uptrends from downtrends.
indicators.rule_in_app: ±5% distance from an SMA saturates that sub-factor's contribution.

indicators.name: RSI (14)
indicators.origin: J. Welles Wilder, 'New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems' (1978)
indicators.what: 0-100 score comparing recent average gains to average losses.
indicators.why: Above 70 traditionally flags an extended run-up ('overbought'); below 30 an extended decline. MarketPulse treats extremes as a momentum-stretch caution, not a signal.
indicators.rule_in_app: ≥70 contributes -0.5 to momentum (stretch risk), ≤30 contributes +0.5 (downside stretch).

indicators.name: MACD (12/26/9)
indicators.what: Gap between fast and slow exponential averages, plus a signal line.
indicators.why: A positive histogram means short-term momentum runs above the longer trend — a directional read.
indicators.rule_in_app: Histogram normalized by ±1% of price before contributing.

indicators.name: Bollinger Bands (20, 2σ)
indicators.why: Bands widen with volatility; prices at the bands are statistically stretched. Shown for context on detail pages.

indicators.name: ATR (14)
indicators.why: Bigger ATR% = bigger typical daily swings = less reliable any single day's direction.
indicators.rule_in_app: ATR ≥ 4% of price contributes strongly to the volatility factor.

indicators.name: Realized Volatility (20d, annualized)
indicators.what: Standard deviation of the last 20 daily returns, annualized.
indicators.why: Above ~28% annualized, outcomes become hard to anticipate — this is exactly what pushes MarketPulse's read toward 'Uncertain'.
indicators.rule_in_app: 12% treated as calm baseline; 42%+ saturates the volatility factor; >28% triggers uncertainty dampening.

indicators.name: OBV (On-Balance Volume)
indicators.what: Cumulative volume added on up-days, subtracted on down-days.
indicators.why: Its slope shows whether volume flows with or against price — the backbone of the volume-pressure proxy.

indicators.name: Up/Down Volume Ratio
indicators.what: Volume on up-days divided by volume on down-days over 10 sessions.

indicators.name: VWAP & VWAP Z-Score
indicators.what: Volume-weighted average price; the z-score measures how many standard deviations today's price sits from its rolling VWAP.
indicators.why: It is a statistical-stretch detector: |z| > 2 means the move is extended versus recent norms.

indicators.name: VIX Velocity
indicators.origin: MarketPulse original (built on the CBOE VIX)
indicators.what: The 5-day change in VIX measured against its own history (z-score).
indicators.why: Fast fear spikes change the risk backdrop before prices do; velocity catches them earlier than level alone.
indicators.rule_in_app: |z| > 1.5 or ±15% in 5 days = volatility regime shift.

indicators.name: Cross-Asset Pressure Matrix
indicators.what: Rolling 60-day correlation of each index against DXY, US 10Y, gold, crude and VIX, plus 5-day lead-lag agreement.
indicators.why: No index moves in isolation — dollar strength, rates and commodities systematically pressure equities. This makes the interaction loop visible to beginners.
indicators.rule_in_app: Correlations and lead agreement are displayed per driver in the Evidence panel.

indicators.name: 52-Week Position
indicators.what: Where price sits between its 52-week low (0%) and high (100%).

indicators.name: Volume vs 20-day Average
indicators.what: Today's volume divided by the 20-day average.
indicators.why: Above-average volume confirms a move's participation; thin volume flags fragility.

honesty_notes: Volume-pressure is a PROXY: real institutional order-flow is private. Public volume data lets us estimate accumulation/distribution pressure, and we label it as an estimate everywhere.
News sentiment is computed from headlines only, with a deterministic keyword fallback when AI is unavailable. Headlines are linked so you can read the sources yourself.
All data carries provenance: which provider served each number and how fresh it is. If live data fails, Demo Mode data is clearly labeled.
Verdicts describe the present, never the future. Every analysis lists 'What would change this read' — the specific conditions that would flip it.

ai_separation.analysis_engine: Generates theses, recap and chat answers from deterministic features only. Prompt-constrained to never advise or predict; every number must come from the provided payload.
ai_separation.pulse_assistant: Explains selected text in simpler words and answers general beginner questions. It never performs analysis, never produces verdicts, and never sees raw data beyond what is on your screen.
ai_separation.shared_rule: Both end every answer with 'Educational information — not investment advice.'
